title: 18 products use unrelated random photographs
actual: Products 4–21 have no image arrays. Each falls back to three Picsum photos labelled as views of that product. These are unrelated scenes, not product documentation.
expected: Every listing has an approved exact-product image, or a clearly labelled representative family image / honest unavailable state.
repro: 390×844 touch viewport; open Products, filter Rims, inspect photographs and alt text. Repeat IDs 4–21 using the inventory.
fix: Prepare approved SKU-to-photo mappings; remove random fallback only in an authorized implementation. Never reuse a different product as an exact photograph.
risk: Wrong mapping can change perceived engineering identity; approval is per SKU.
accept: All 21 products have approved media status, meaningful alt, and no random-scene fallback.

title: SKU-001 name and photograph describe different products
actual: The record says Box Frame Bearing & Racer; all three mapped assets depict and label a red Heavy Duty Frame. The alt repeats Heavy Duty Frame. This is a confirmed association mismatch, not proof of which product name is correct.
expected: Name, exact product photo, alt, specifications and enquiry context refer to the same client-approved item.
repro: 390×844; tap the first product title, advance the carousel and compare the frame image with the bearing/racer heading.
fix: Client chooses the authoritative identity and genuine media. Retain all existing masters until that decision; do not rename or reshape engineering features speculatively.
risk: A name-only change could break client catalogue alignment.
accept: Client signs off the SKU identity; all three views and enquiry text agree.

title: Factory, people and sustainability captions accompany placeholder scenes
actual: All 15 Gallery URLs are Picsum. Rendered Factory Floor Overview shows a beach. About has two Picsum leadership portraits; Mission and Sustainability also attach real-world captions to random imagery. Editorial images are random too.
expected: Factual factory/person captions use authorized genuine photography. Editorial illustrations are clearly distinguished.
repro: 390×844 and 1440×900; inspect Gallery first card and About leadership; compare captions with visible scenes.
fix: Use a location/person/content approval register and replace only with approved assets. Gemini may later supply labelled conceptual process or editorial illustrations, never documentary factory or certificate evidence.
risk: Removing placeholder imagery without layout reservations can introduce shifts.
accept: Every factual image has provenance and a matching caption; illustrative media is labelled.

title: Forms can claim delivery without sending anything
actual: Read-only handlers prevent default and immediately set success state. Contact promises Message Sent and a response; Careers says Application Received. No delivery call is present. No form was submitted during this audit.
expected: Visitors receive truthful availability and delivery feedback; success appears only after confirmed delivery in a separately authorized integration.
evidence: evidence/contact-390-en.png; evidence/careers-form-390.png; static handlers cited below
repro: Static reproduction: follow each handleSubmit to setIsSubmitted / setSubmitted. Do not submit live data.
fix: Approve an honest public unavailable/demo state and verified alternate contact first; plan delivery separately. Do not implement backend, authentication or notifications within UI polish.
risk: Changing success copy must preserve the approved future form workflow.
effort: 0.5 day for truthful UI; delivery separately scoped
accept: No public UI promises sent/received before actual acknowledgement; pending/error/unavailable states are distinguishable.

title: Download buttons have no document targets
actual: Clicking a Downloads card produced zero download events and zero requests. Its button has no handler or URL. Home 2026 Catalog and Downloads featured Download Now are also inert; product Download Spec Sheet only opens the generic Downloads page.
expected: Each promised file action opens the correct approved document or clearly states that it is unavailable.
repro: 390×844; click first Download on Downloads and observe no file or navigation. Inspect Home 2026 Catalog and the drawer spec-sheet destination.
fix: Request the 11 listed files and approved metadata; map real URLs individually. Use an explicit unavailable state until approved files exist.
risk: Do not publish internal QC or CAD documents merely because a seed advertises them.
accept: Every enabled download retrieves the advertised MIME type, filename and version; no inert enabled control.

title: Desktop navigation dropdowns cannot be opened by keyboard
actual: Quality, Company and Media triggers are DIVs with mouse enter/leave only and no tabindex or role. Pointer hover opens the dropdown; Tab cannot focus its trigger.
expected: Keyboard and pointer users can open the same menus and reach every link.
repro: 1440×900; Tab through header. Compare with hovering Quality.
fix: Use real disclosure buttons with expanded state, keyboard opening/closing and predictable focus, preserving the approved menu appearance.
risk: Pointer hover and focus transitions must not close a menu while moving to a link.
accept: Tab reaches triggers; Enter/Space opens; Escape closes; links remain operable by pointer and keyboard.

title: Product, gallery and vacancy cards lack keyboard triggers
actual: Primary card actions are click handlers on DIVs without role/tabindex. Product View Details is a non-interactive span. Carousel buttons remain tabbable but cannot open product details.
expected: A named keyboard-operable control opens each item without nesting interactive carousel controls inside a button.
repro: 390×844 and desktop width; use Tab then Enter to try to open product, gallery or job details.
fix: Give titles/details actions real button/link semantics and a visible focus state; preserve separate carousel controls.
risk: Avoid nested buttons and double activation when carousel arrows bubble.
accept: Every item opens by keyboard; arrows only change images; mobile tap behaviour remains unchanged.

title: Drawers and overlays do not manage modal focus
actual: Product opening leaves focus on BODY and has no dialog role. Shift+Tab from its Close button reaches background pagination/carousel controls. Mobile menu focus stays on its background opener. Gallery has no scroll lock and the page moved from y=53 to y=553 behind the lightbox.
expected: Blocking overlays have an accessible name, an intentional initial focus, contained keyboard focus, inert background and opener restoration.
repro: 390×844; open a product, focus Close and Shift+Tab; open Gallery and wheel behind it; open mobile Menu and inspect activeElement.
fix: Adopt one small accessible dialog/drawer primitive after approval; specify scroll locking, focus return, accessible name and background inertness.
risk: Products already locks body and closes with Escape; preserve these behaviours and safe-area sizing.
accept: Repeated Tab/Shift+Tab stays inside; close returns to opener; background is not actionable; screen reader announces a named dialog.

title: Escape closing is inconsistent
actual: Escape closes Products, but Gallery lightbox, Careers drawer and mobile menu stayed open in executed tests.
expected: The same documented keyboard dismissal works for equivalent blocking overlays.
repro: 390×844; open each overlay and press Escape; compare with Products.
fix: Implement Escape consistently through the approved shared overlay primitive, with a visible Close control and focus restoration.
risk: Do not close multiple stacked overlays from one keypress.
accept: Escape closes only the top overlay and restores its opener.

title: Visible form labels are not associated with fields
actual: All six Contact fields have labels.length=0. Subject select has no accessible name (axe select-name). Careers name/email/phone have neither associated labels nor aria-label. Placeholder text does not repair the visible label relationship.
expected: Every field has a persistent, programmatically associated label and understandable required/error state.
repro: 390×844; inspect labels on Contact and the job form. Clicking a visible label should focus its field; run axe with drawer open after the fix.
fix: Assign stable IDs and htmlFor, accessible error descriptions and name/role state; retain native required/email constraints.
risk: IDs must remain unique across public forms and open overlays.
accept: Each field has one correct label; Subject and job inputs pass naming checks; errors link to the correct field.
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value

title: Product enquiry is classified as General Inquiry
actual: The product name is correctly inserted into Message, but Subject displays General Inquiry. State is assigned Product Inquiry: <name>, which matches no select option.
expected: Subject displays Product Inquiry while preserving the exact selected product in the message/context.
repro: 390×844; tap first product title, tap Request Inquiry, inspect Subject and Message without submitting.
fix: Use an existing stable subject value and a separate product context; validate query context without inventing specifications.
risk: Preserve user edits if query parameters change after typing.
accept: Every product enquiry opens with visible Product Inquiry and correct product text; manual subject changes persist.

title: Bengali mode leaves most public content in English
actual: All 22 Bengali route states set html lang=bn and load the Bengali font, but Products, forms and most page bodies remain hardcoded English. Home also mixes Bengali heading with English copy and Explore Catalog. About retains English fragments and numeric milestone logic tests a missing i18n_lang key.
expected: Approved translated content and correct language-of-parts declarations; untranslated content is honestly identified.
repro: 390×844; select Bengali then open Products/Contact/Mission. Compare document language and visible content.
fix: Inventory hardcoded strings, obtain native-reader/client translations and mark remaining English passages lang=en. Preserve the approved Bengali font pending reader testing.
risk: Long translations can change menu, hero and button wrapping.
accept: Critical product/enquiry journeys are translated and tested at 320–430px; language parts are declared; no broken Bengali clusters.
wcag: 3.1.2 Language of Parts; translation completeness is also a product requirement

title: Subtle text and faded timelines fail contrast
actual: Axe reports #94a3b8 on white at 2.56:1 for 12px product SKUs, below 4.5:1. Faded timeline years and labels add further failures. The 22 mobile scans contain 361 violation nodes including repeated shared elements, not 361 unique defects.
expected: Normal text meets 4.5:1; large text meets 3:1; meaningful UI boundaries meet the applicable non-text requirement.
repro: 390×844; inspect product SKU text and timeline years; repeat contrast calculations using final composited colours.
fix: Introduce accessible text roles and limit decorative fading to nonessential graphics. Keep semantic success/error colours; do not make every hover red.
risk: Changing a shared colour may affect badges, borders and icon contrast.
accept: All reported text contrast failures are resolved or documented decorative exceptions; both locales and overlays checked.

title: Card and article text undercuts the approved readability baseline
actual: Product names are 16px and body 14px, editorial card excerpts 12px, Downloads descriptions 13px/metadata 10px, article/legal body 15px. DESIGN.md specifies body 18–20px and small text 14–16px. Numerous font-light overrides also contradict its guidance.
expected: Use agreed readable body/card roles; justified small metadata remains legible without blindly forcing large fixed sizes on 320px screens.
repro: 390×844 and 1440×900; compare Products/Blog/Downloads and legal body to design typography roles.
fix: Agree a small fluid type scale, then apply by semantic role. Review Bengali line-height and Latin fallback before changing font families.
risk: Larger text can increase truncation and card height; recheck enquiry/footer lengths.
accept: Body copy meets the approved scale or has a documented exception; long titles remain discoverable at 320px and enlarged text.

title: Global reset overrides rounded button styles
actual: Unlayered button { border-radius: inherit; } overrides layered Tailwind rounded utilities. Computed Product arrows, filters, Menu and chat radius is 0px despite rounded-full/rounded-lg classes. Screenshots show square controls; .btn-primary has its own later rule and retains 8px.
expected: Buttons render the radius assigned by their intended variant consistently.
repro: 390×844; inspect computed border-radius for Next image, Open chat, Menu and Filter by All.
fix: Scope or place the reset in the correct layer in an approved CSS-only batch, then verify computed styles instead of only class strings.
risk: The reset is global; audit any affected public button and avoid unrequested Admin edits.
accept: Carousel/chat shapes and filter/menu radii match approved tokens; .btn variants remain unchanged.

title: Equivalent heroes and content containers use different scales
actual: Products/About use clamp(52px,9vw,120px); Contact uses clamp(40px,7vw,96px); several pages reach 9rem (144px) versus DESIGN maximum 72px. Containers mix container-premium with container + px-6/md:px-12/lg:px-24; body and hero subtitle roles vary.
expected: A small documented set of hero/content variants preserves intentional hierarchy without arbitrary scale drift.
repro: Compare equivalent heroes at 390 and 1440px; measure heading size, inset, section padding and title wrapping.
fix: Agree hero variants, content widths and spacing tokens. Do not enlarge the narrow-phone Navbar or force 72px headings where they would overflow.
risk: A blanket utility replacement would erase approved page-specific composition.
accept: Equivalent page roles share a reviewed scale; all deviations are named/justified; no new overflow.

title: Secondary-page heroes delay access to the main task on mobile
actual: At 390px the Product filter starts around y=689 and first image around y=860; Contact form starts around y=974. Multiple decorative rules, mb-10 gaps and stat strips consume much of the first viewport. Full mobile pages reach 5,810–10,067px in several cases.
expected: The main product/contact task appears promptly while retaining the approved visual character. Exact whitespace reduction is a design recommendation, not a WCAG failure by itself.
repro: 390×844; count scroll needed to search Products and start a Contact message; compare hero section sizes.
fix: Review compact mobile secondary-page hero variants; keep homepage storytelling and intentional inner scrollers. Validate task access with the owner before changing spacing.
risk: Removing all whitespace would violate the approved premium direction.
accept: At 390px product search is visible early and contact entry requires less avoidable scrolling; before/after owner review required.

title: Valid article pages render an empty document title
actual: Direct navigation repeatedly yields document.title="" and an empty title element alongside the original static title. Axe document-title fails for each sampled valid detail route. The visible H1 still renders.
expected: Each valid article has one meaningful browser title containing its headline and company name.
repro: 390×844; directly load each sampled valid detail route and inspect document.title / all title elements after load.
fix: Investigate React 19/Helmet metadata ownership and pass a single composed title string; verify direct and client navigation. The exact underlying library interaction needs a controlled fix test.
risk: Avoid duplicate metadata while preserving social/structured content.
accept: Exactly one nonempty correct title after direct load, SPA navigation and back/forward for all valid detail IDs.
status: Confirmed; exact library cause not proven

title: Fallback pages keep generic indexable metadata
actual: Missing articles render only a paragraph and back link, with no H1 or route metadata. Wildcard has an H1 but uses the generic title/description and index,follow. Local preview serves the SPA shell with HTTP 200; deployed unknown-route status was not checked.
expected: Missing states are clearly titled and semantically structured; production status/indexing policy is deliberate.
repro: Load a nonnumeric ID, 9999 and /audit-missing-page; inspect title, H1 and robots.
fix: Add a consistent public missing-content component and metadata; separately plan real static/HTTP status handling without changing hosting in this audit.
risk: A noindex rule must not leak to valid pages during navigation.
accept: Missing states have a descriptive title/H1 and reviewed indexing policy; valid pages recover correct metadata.

title: Metadata/domain strategy is unresolved and fragmented
actual: Static and Helmet descriptions coexist (two on valid sampled detail pages). Canonicals and sitemap use www.modinarim.com although two deployment domains are supplied. Sitemap omits Gallery, Careers, FAQ and detail URLs. OG/Twitter images are relative and generic; initial HTML has an empty root and generic metadata.
expected: One approved canonical origin, one route-owned metadata set, an accurate public sitemap and reliable share previews.
repro: Inspect direct detail DOM head, dist/index.html and sitemap. Compare deployment URL to canonical; do not assume an unapproved domain is wrong.
fix: Obtain production-domain decision, consolidate metadata, use absolute approved share images and plan public pre-rendering separately. No framework rewrite is required just for metadata cleanup.
risk: Premature canonical changes can split search identity; do not change hosting/domain settings.
effort: 1–2 days for frontend; static rendering separately estimated
accept: One correct title/description/canonical per valid route; sitemap covers approved URLs; invalid routes excluded; share URLs resolve on approved origin.

title: Certificate evidence needs renewed documents and entity confirmation
actual: The inspected ISO 9001 image names Modina Metal Industries, not Modina Rim & Parts Ltd.; it shows surveillance/certificate-expiry 09 April 2024 and recertification due 09 April 2026. Audit date is 27 October 2026. Website text presents current triple certification and a 2025–2026 renewal article. The image discrepancy is confirmed; current legal validity and entity relationship are unverified.
expected: Public certification claims are supported by current approved documents for the correct legal entity and product scope.
repro: Compare certificate entity and dated fields with page/company wording. Client/issuer verification is required; no issuer was contacted.
fix: Client supplies renewed certificates, surveillance status, entity relationship and publication permission. Do not declare certification invalid or alter the document image based only on this audit.
risk: Unsupported edits could misrepresent a legal entity or certification scope.
accept: Every public claim maps to current approved evidence; entity/date/scope are consistent across pages and metadata.
status: Confirmed document discrepancy; client verification required

title: Public telephone numbers disagree
routes: Navbar, mobile drawer, /contact, /products, footer, Organization JSON-LD
actual: Header/tap-to-call uses +8801321234510; mobile drawer/footer/Contact/Product sales and Home structured data use the different +8801234567890 pattern. The correct client number was not verified or dialled.
expected: Every contact channel uses the client-approved number and a valid tel link.
repro: 390×844; compare top call button, mobile drawer Sales CTA and Contact detail. Read JSON-LD without calling.
fix: Obtain one approved contact register and reuse it in public display, tel links, metadata and footer. Keep the full-number narrow-phone layout.
risk: Do not assume the plausible-looking header number is authoritative.
accept: All intended sales contact occurrences agree with the signed-off register; no real call required for UI regression.

title: Business claims and identity assets lack supplied approval evidence
actual: Hardcoded testimonials use stock portraits and named companies; production capacity, tolerance, materials, availability, MOQ, lead time, export/CSR milestones and workforce claims are asserted. Contact includes explicit placeholder office addresses. No client evidence was supplied for these claims.
expected: Marketing and commercial assertions have traceable client approval; placeholders are not mistaken for factual company evidence.
repro: Read Home testimonials, Product spec drawer, Sustainability statistics, News and Contact locations. This is verification inventory, not a finding that all claims are false.
fix: Build a client sign-off register for identity, commercial terms, capabilities, testimonials/consent and rights. Preserve source conflicts for decisions.
risk: Editing specs or company history without approval can create new inaccuracies.
effort: 1–2 days for register; client review external
accept: Every published factual claim has an owner, evidence/status and approved wording; no invented replacement facts.
status: Client-verification requirement; not a confirmed falsehood

title: News featured story opens a different article
actual: Featured card says April 2026 catalogue launch; Read Article links to articlesData[0], the March 2026 ISO renewal story. The detail title does not match the promised story.
expected: A featured story opens matching headline/date/body, or clearly links to an appropriate alternative destination.
repro: 390×844 or 1440×900; read featured headline, follow Read Article and compare the article H1.
fix: Client approves a real detail record/destination; bind featured presentation to that record rather than unrelated first-list item.
risk: Do not invent a launch article solely to make the link match.
accept: Featured headline/date/image and destination article describe the same approved event.

title: News list and detail disagree on the same person
actual: News item 7 names Mohammed Rafiqul Islam in the listing; NewsDetail item 7 names Md. Faruq Hossain. This is a source-confirmed conflict, not a verified identity.
expected: One approved person name is used consistently in summaries and full text.
repro: Inspect item 7 in both source arrays; this detail item was not separately rendered.
fix: Obtain client decision, then share approved editorial records between list and detail without changing routing.
risk: Blindly choosing the detail name would overwrite a source conflict.
accept: Listing/detail/metadata use the approved identity; no unrelated article changes.

title: Large source media are served without responsive variants
actual: Product views are roughly 1.46–2.04 MB each, certificates roughly 1.71–1.78 MB each. public/logo.jpg is a 7.94 MB 12,500² favicon target. hero.jpg is 8.61 MB (social image, not the rotating hero asset). There are exact duplicate source/public masters; they are not all downloaded on every page.
expected: Small rendered slots receive suitable optimized variants while authentic masters are preserved.
repro: Compare on-disk bytes/dimensions against 4:3 card slots and 220px certificate previews. Inspect favicon reference.
fix: After media approval, produce responsive WebP/AVIF/JPEG variants, srcset/sizes and a small favicon. Preserve masters; share equivalent certificate URLs where appropriate.
risk: Compression must preserve engineering annotations and certificate legibility.
accept: Correct responsive variants are transferred; visual detail preserved; favicon is appropriately sized; no master deleted.

title: Eager public bundle and cold rendering are costly
actual: Build emits 1,109.11 kB public JS (283.91 kB gzip) and 88.02 kB CSS; Vite warns about chunk size. Public pages are eager imports. Synthetic cold LCP observations are 12.396s Home, 9.560s Products, 9.140s Contact in an uncompressed local preview under the recorded throttle. These are single lab samples, not field scores.
expected: The first route loads only necessary code and renders promptly on the agreed mobile network budget.
repro: Run the recorded production build and CDP test; compare the large initial script request with render timing.
fix: Profile route-level splitting and defer optional chatbot code; establish image/code budgets and repeat controlled lab tests. Vite injects a browser AI key when configured: treat safe public-chat availability as a separate existing architecture decision, without exposing values or implementing backend here.
risk: Splitting can change route transitions/preloader behaviour; missing-key AI status must be truthful.
effort: 1–2 days frontend performance; integration separately scoped
accept: Initial JS is measurably reduced; lab LCP improves under repeatable conditions; field INP is measured only when actual field data exists.

title: Fixed preloader adds delay and clips narrow-screen branding
routes: All public routes on fresh session
actual: Source runs a 2.2s counter + 0.4s hold + 0.8s exit regardless of network readiness. It was gone at a follow-up capture after a subsequent four-second wait; exact wall-clock completion was not measured. At 320px each half is 160px with 32px side padding; the brand text is visibly clipped. This is an entry-animation issue, not document overflow.
expected: Entry feedback does not hide useful content unnecessarily and remains legible at narrow widths.
repro: Fresh 320×740 context with no modina_loaded key; capture during the counter and wait for completion.
fix: Review a short/skip/reduced-motion path and mobile-safe brand layout; preserve the visual concept subject to owner approval.
risk: Session behaviour and initial route visibility must remain deterministic.
accept: 320px brand text is visible; reduced-motion has a minimal path; loading feedback is not a fixed unnecessary gate.

title: Hero keeps rotating with no pause, including reduced-motion mode
actual: Home advances every 5s indefinitely with prev/next/dots but no pause control. With prefers-reduced-motion=reduce, recorded src still changed from hero_products to hero_rims. Source videos autoplay+loop without controls; actual playback was paused in the sampled hidden/below-fold state.
expected: Visitors can pause auto-updating content; reduced-motion preferences are respected.
repro: Emulate reduced motion; wait >5s and compare hero src. Inspect controls and autoplay source.
fix: Add accessible pause/play and reduced-motion behaviour; defer below-fold video and provide an intentional still state. Do not claim every CSS animation is an AA violation.
risk: Manual navigation should not unexpectedly resume paused rotation.
accept: Pause stops rotation, manual selection works, reduced-motion starts static, and any playing loop can be stopped.
status: Confirmed hero issue; video control gap source-confirmed

title: Images and icon-only links/buttons lack meaningful names
actual: Axe reports four missing image alts on About (company and leadership), one each on Sustainability and featured News/Blog. Four footer social links are unnamed on every route and point to #. Five Home testimonial controls are unnamed.
expected: Informative images have appropriate alt; decorative images have empty alt; every interactive icon has a useful name and real destination.
repro: Run the recorded 390px axe scan; inspect image-alt, link-name and button-name nodes.
fix: Approve captions/links, add semantic names and appropriate alt. Do not label random photos as actual employees; unavailable socials should not appear functional.
risk: Blindly duplicating nearby text as alt can make navigation verbose.
accept: No image-alt/link-name/button-name failures remain for public states; all enabled social links have approved destinations.
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content; 2.4.4 Link Purpose; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value

title: Homepage progress dots are too small and tightly spaced
actual: Hero progress buttons are 3px high; inactive widths are 16px with 4px gaps. Testimonial dots are 6px high with 8px gaps. Adjacent small targets do not have 24px separation. Product carousel indicators are already 32×32 and should be retained.
expected: Pointer targets meet WCAG 2.2 AA minimum size or its spacing/equivalent-control exceptions; aim for practical 44px mobile targets.
repro: 390×844; measure actual button rectangles, not just visible dots. Apply spacing exceptions rather than declaring all sub-44px controls failures.
fix: Keep tiny visual markers inside larger transparent button hit areas; label selected state and retain prev/next alternatives.
risk: Expanded hit areas must not overlap image arrows or captions.
accept: Marker visuals remain restrained; actual targets meet 24px/spacing requirements and are comfortable to tap.
status: Confirmed dimensions; assess equivalent-control exception per function

title: Accordion and most category controls omit state semantics
actual: FAQ answers open visually, but question buttons expose no aria-expanded or aria-controls. Products correctly uses aria-pressed; other category bars largely use styling only and are inconsistent.
expected: Assistive technology receives the same expanded/selected state visible to sighted users.
repro: 390×844; open first FAQ and inspect attributes; compare Products category semantics with other filter bars.
fix: Add stable accordion relationships and consistent filter button pressed state; announce result changes without stealing input focus.
risk: Do not introduce tablist semantics unless the complete keyboard pattern is implemented.
accept: Expanded and selected states are programmatically exposed; dynamic counts are understandable; controls still work by tap/keyboard.
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 4.1.3 Status Messages where applicable

title: Global product search loses exact-item intent
actual: Searching Wasar returns a named result, but its link opens only /products?category=Hardware with three cards and no drawer. Search can match product descriptions but does not carry the original term or selected ID.
expected: A chosen product result reveals that product clearly, preserving search intent.
repro: 390×844; open Search, enter Wasar, select the result; inspect resulting URL/cards.
fix: Choose a minimal public query contract for selected product/search term; preserve category-only footer links. Document product permalink requirements separately.
risk: Query changes must not break existing approved category URLs.
accept: Selecting any search result makes the exact product immediately identifiable; back/forward and existing category links remain correct.

title: Image request failures leave empty/broken product frames
actual: No onError fallback appears in the shared carousel. Aborted Picsum requests create broken image states with no honest unavailable message. Many remote dependencies have no local content fallback.
expected: Unavailable media reserves geometry and communicates the problem without misrepresenting the product.
repro: Block Picsum requests in the local browser, filter Rims and inspect images. This simulates an outage; it is not proof of a current public-host outage.
fix: Add a stable reserved image frame with approved unavailable text and retry as appropriate; prioritize locally owned optimized assets.
risk: Do not replace failed exact photos with misleading random scenes.
accept: Failed/slow images do not collapse layout or show misleading alt scenes; gallery/product actions remain usable.

title: Catalogue counts do not match the local data
actual: Products advertises 4 Categories but has three data categories (Motorcycle 6, Rims 12, Hardware 3). News advertises 12+ Articles but the source contains eight list entries plus a separate featured block. Downloads similarly repeats four product categories and exposes a Certificates filter with no certificate records.
expected: Counts and filter labels describe actual available content; distinct marketing families are labelled separately.
repro: Compare visible stats/filter counts with the public arrays; choose Certificates on Downloads after implementation tests.
fix: Derive catalogue counts from source records; obtain client decision on genuinely missing articles/documents instead of inventing content.
risk: Four homepage visual families may remain valid if clearly distinguished from catalogue categories.
accept: Displayed record counts match approved data; empty categories have a clear state and no promised unavailable files.

title: Certificate previews cannot be enlarged or downloaded
actual: Certificate images sit in 220px contain frames (Certificates) with opacity 0.7 until hover. Cards use cursor-default and no lightbox/open-original action. Text on a full 2550×3300 certificate is not readable in that thumbnail; mobile has no persistent hover.
expected: Visitors can open a legible approved document with keyboard/touch controls and clear issue/validity information.
repro: 390×844 and 1440×900; try to enlarge or open a certificate, compare legibility to original.
fix: After entity/date approval, add a clear view-document action and accessible preview or actual file link; keep full image legibility.
risk: Do not make outdated documents more prominent before approval.
accept: Approved certificate can be read at useful size and dismissed/accessed by keyboard and touch.

title: Careers fields use a different shape and focus pattern
actual: Contact uses filled bordered rounded fields; Careers uses transparent bottom-border fields with rounded-none and outline-none. This diverges from DESIGN 56px/8px fields and weakens the common visual/focus system.
expected: Public inputs share a deliberate visual, label, height and focus convention, with justified textarea/compact exceptions.
repro: 390×844; compare Contact and job form controls and tab focus.
fix: Reuse a minimal public field style with label/error wiring; verify visible focus rather than relying solely on border-colour change.
risk: Do not import or modify Admin form components during this public-only batch.
accept: Equivalent inputs share approved radius/height/focus; mobile text stays at least 16px; textareas remain comfortable.

title: Bypass navigation and heading structure can be improved
actual: No visible-on-focus skip link is present. Products goes from H1 to card H3s without a grid H2; other pages use decorative and metadata H4s. A main landmark already exists and should be kept.
expected: Keyboard users can reach main content efficiently; headings describe a coherent content outline.
repro: Tab from page start and review the DOM heading list, using native assistive-technology review in a later gate.
fix: Add a focus-visible skip link and descriptive grid heading where appropriate; do not label every metadata item as a heading.
risk: Skip destination must account for fixed header and remain focusable.
accept: First keyboard action offers main-content access and public heading outlines have a reviewed hierarchy.
status: Recommendation; not a blanket WCAG failure

title: Dark CTAs and bespoke effects diverge from the light baseline
routes: Many secondary pages; homepage category media
actual: Several full-width CTA sections use bg-modina-heading with white text; DESIGN explicitly says never dark. Existing category art is predominantly black/red and uses heavy shadows. The approved current identity contains this conflict, so changing all of it automatically would be inappropriate.
expected: Owner explicitly resolves which existing dark accents are approved exceptions to DESIGN, with a minimal consistent policy.
repro: Compare DESIGN light-interface rules with secondary-page CTA sections and existing category images.
fix: Document approved exceptions first; standardize only the agreed public CTA/media presentation, retaining the brand-red/light overall direction.
risk: A broad colour replacement could erase approved composition and reduce image contrast.
accept: Owner signs off exception policy; equivalent CTA variants follow it consistently.
status: Confirmed baseline conflict; visual remedy needs owner decision

title: Mobile product detail affordance is hover-only
actual: At a touch-oriented 390px viewport, View Details has computed opacity 0 until group hover. The card remains tappable by pointer but does not expose the text cue; keyboard access is separately blocked by PUB-007.
expected: Mobile visitors see a clear, always-available details action and feedback for activation.
